text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert P-74321 fired for service=hosted-inference-prod (error-rate > 5%, 5m window). Escalation policy infra-oncall: primary @chris -> secondary @sam -> manager @maria. Primary did not ack within 60s, routing to secondary.

chris: I never received the phone page. Phone says DND, weird. I can try to ack from web but can't find the incident ID in my mobile PD app.

sam: I got an SMS but no voice page. SMS has link that times out. Trying to ack via web now... acked (P-74321)

ops-bot: Note: incident created automatically by monitoring. Active alerts: 3 hosts reporting 502s from inference runtime. Recent deploys: none in last 6h.

marta: Quick context — we're seeing a spike in 502/503 from inference workers in us-west-2; frontend retries are backing up and causing queue growth. Impact: non-SLA customers experiencing request failures and ~40% increase in end-to-end latency.

alex: On it. Triage steps: 1) confirm affected pool (inference-pool-a), 2) check GPU-driver logs, 3) open bridge for real-time coordination. Opening bridge now. Bridge: https://zoom.us/j/987654321 (pw: infer123)

chris: I can join but my mobile notifications are flaky. I'll use the bridge.

incident-bot: Escalation window expired for secondary; manager escalation fired to @maria because secondary ack didn't have confirmed response within 5m.

maria: I'm up, joining bridge. Sam — are you still seeing the incident in PD as acknowledged? If so we should either escalate to manager bridge or create a Pager phone-bridge.

sam: Ack still in my PD. I clicked "ack" but nothing changed in the incident notes. Might be PD UI glitch.

tilly: Jumping in — oncall takeover in 20m if this persists. What's the mitigation plan?

marta: Short-term mitigation: divert traffic to model variant v1-small (lower memory footprint) and scale up a hot pool. Running router config change now. Command: `curl -X POST https://router.internal/api/v1/route -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ROUTER_TOKEN' -d '{"spill_to":"v1-small","percent":40}'`

alex: Running `kubectl get pods -n inference --selector=pool=inference-pool-a -o wide`
```
NAME                                READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
inf-worker-5c9d7d6c8b-6j9t2        1/1     Running   0          3d
inf-worker-5c9d7d6c8b-7kqz1        0/1     CrashLoop 5          2m
inf-worker-5c9d7d6c8b-8h2md        1/1     Running   0          3d
```

alex: Seeing a recent CrashLoop on one replica; logs show OOM in the inference binary. `kubectl logs inf-worker-5c9d7d6c8b-7kqz1 -n inference` shows repeated kvcache allocation failures.

marta: That aligns with increased memory pressure. Suggest immediate pod restart + scale up by 2 replicas while we investigate memory leak. Command: `kubectl scale deployment inf-worker --replicas=6 -n inference` and `kubectl rollout restart deployment/inf-worker -n inference`.

sam: Scaled and restarted. New pods coming up.

incident-bot: PagerDuty note appended: "Mitigation started: traffic spill to v1-small (40%), scaled inf-worker to 6 replicas, new bridge opened."

chris: Confirmed traffic spill succeeded; frontend error-rate down from 5.2% -> 1.1% over last 3m. Still monitoring.

maria: Good. Customer impact estimate: ~3000 requests failed in the last 15m, primarily from enterprise customers on heavy prompt lengths (>2k tokens). Recommend manual outreach to top 5 affected accounts after stabilization.

tilly: I'll draft the outreach and coordinate with CS. Also adding a temporary runway in infra-oncall policy to extend secondary timeout to 3m for this window — reduces manager escalation storms while infra stabilizes.

sam: Note: PD mobile notifications still flaky for me; I had to use web UI. Raising a support ticket with PD: https://support.pagerduty.com/ticket/INC-9999

ops-bot: PD support ticket created and linked to incident.

alex: After restarts, new pods booted cleanly. Memory usage for pool now within normal range. Monitoring shows 95% healthy within 6m of mitigation.

marta: Next steps: revert spill to v1-small gradually once stable, run postmortem to root cause the kvcache allocation spike, add additional guardrails to prevent memory exhaustion (cgroup limits, OOM handler restart thresholds), and review PagerDuty mobile delivery for primary/secondary.

incident-bot: Incident P-74321 status: Mitigated -> Monitoring. All actions logged. Manager notified.

chris: Thanks team. I'm logging follow-ups in the incident timeline. If anything regresses ping me directly.

tilly: Taking handoff. I'll be on watch for 2h and will update with a short incident summary and action items for the postmortem. Closing coordination in this thread — follow-up thread for postmortem planning will be created. :white_check_mark:

maria: Assigning owners: postmortem lead @marta, PD delivery follow-up @sam, customer outreach @tilly.

sam: ack.

marta: ack.

incident-bot: Incident P-74321 auto-update: Postmortem draft template created at /docs/incidents/P-74321-draft.md.

tilly: copying the bridge notes and timeline into the doc now.

chris: Closing my involvement. Good job on quick mitigation everyone.
